latest_release.body:
All 81 npm cohort packages are available as version 2.0.5 on `latest`. The source is `c094a549fee09f6e06911b8486b9789b536401aa` from `develop`.

Use exact versions to install this release:

```sh
npm install @elizaos/core@2.0.5
npm install @elizaos/agent@2.0.5
```

The public tarball bytes, sizes, package names, versions, source IDs and publisher records matched the immutable release plan for all 81 packages. The attached plan is the original plan. The attached validation record gives the observation times, package hashes and evidence hashes.

This GitHub record uses a manual metadata recovery lane. Canonical workflow run 43049531373, attempt 6, failed after npm publication and `latest` promotion. npm rejected a DELETE request for the temporary candidate alias with HTTP 403. At the last byte-audit observation, all 81 candidate aliases still pointed to 2.0.5. This recovery leaves npm and those aliases untouched. The canonical workflow and transaction state remain failed or incomplete. This record does not claim that all checks passed.

The public consumer check passed Core install, dependency tree and compiled import. Agent install and CLI version also passed. The Agent dependency tree returned exit code 1: React 19.3.1 failed a peer range, and 15 packages were reported as extraneous. No provider calls, full Agent startup, native capabilities or device acceptance were checked.

Desktop publication was disabled. The Snap Store, Microsoft Store, and Google Play and Apple App Store jobs were skipped. This is an npm release; this metadata recovery does not publish desktop installers or store builds.

The complete [GitHub-generated repository change list](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/v2.0.5/full-changelog.md) is attached. GitHub generated it at 2026-11-11 22:12:20 UTC and selected `pr-evidence-14` as the comparison base for `v2.0.5`. The [full comparison](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/compare/pr-evidence-14...v2.0.5) preserves that scope. Package and runtime qualification evidence is in `package-validation.json`.

detail.readme:
elizaOS

Your agentic operating system.

Eliza · Eliza Cloud · elizaOS downloads · Documentation

elizaOS is an open-source TypeScript framework and product stack for autonomous AI agents. This monorepo contains the core runtime, the Eliza app, the CLI, cloud services, native bridges, and first-party plugins. Android distribution tooling lives in [`packages/os`](packages/os/README.md). ## Choose a starting point | Goal | Start here | | --- | --- | | Use Eliza | [Open the web app](https://cloud.eliza.app), visit [Eliza downloads](https://eliza.app/downloads), or use a published [GitHub release](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases) | | Run this repository | Follow [Run Eliza from source](#run-eliza-from-source) | | Build an agent or plugin | Start with [the runtime](#build-an-agent) and the [developer docs](https://docs.elizaos.ai/) | | Contribute | Read the [required contribution rules](#contributing) and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | | Run a whole device as elizaOS | Start with the build requirements and target guides in [`packages/os`](packages/os/README.md) | ## Run Eliza from source The repository pins Bun and Node versions in [`package.json`](package.json). Install Bun, then: ```bash git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/elizaos/eliza.git cd eliza bun install bun run dev ``` `bun install` also prepares submodules and patches, provisions supported host build prerequisites, and builds or verifies the staged desktop `libelizainference`. The embedding GGUF remains runtime-managed and downloads automatically during local-inference warmup. Fetch archived artifact fixtures explicitly with `bun packages/scripts/fetch-archive-artifacts.ts` when needed. Common repository commands: ```bash bun run dev:local # app + API with the runtime chooser (local agent, own provider keys; Cloud sign-in not required) bun run start # run the standalone agent host (API only, no UI; use bun run dev for the app) bun run build # build the workspace with Turbo bun run verify # dependency, type, lint, and audit gates bun run test:quint # application state models and invariants bun run test # repository end-to-end test lane bun run test:e2e # end-to-end lane bun run cloud:mock # local Eliza Cloud stack with mocks ``` Package build/test commands are in each package's README.
